text:
Cara: FYI I'm seeing a systematic +12% delta between invoice_preview and final across a few preview tenants this morning (window 2026-06-14T01:00..03:00). Sample tenant: lunar-works.

Viktor: Any quick leads? preview vs final usually due to aggregation dedupe differences or SKU token_factor mismatches.

Samir: Looked at a trace: req_id=r-373-01 produced two partials in preview because router rewrote route_tag mid-flight (preview->fallback) and tagged the second partial with route_priority='low' so preview merged both under separate buckets. Final billing dedupes by req_id and collapses to single.

Mina: can you paste the event envelope?

Samir: pasted minimal: ```json
{"req_id":"r-373-01","tenant":"lunar-works","route_tag":"preview-canary","model_requested":"gptx-4","model_served":"gptx-4-small-quant","tokens_in":250,"tokens_out":850}
```
Preview aggregates: partial A (sampling_id=s-42, route_tag=preview-canary, tokens=900), partial B (sampling_id=null, route_tag=fallback, tokens=200) -> preview summed -> 1100. Final replay dedupe -> 900.

Viktor: Ok two issues: (1) sampling_id gets nulled on fallback path, (2) preview merge logic unions sampling buckets by model_alias+route_tag which allows double-counting when fallback happens.

Cara: Why is sampling_id null on fallback? Recent deploys?
deploy-bot: Deployed router v6.1.0 at 2026-06-13T23:50Z. Change: canonicalize model_alias and collapse route_tags for simpler routing; optimization accidentally drops sampling_id when applying fallback rewrite. Link: https://ci.redwood/router/6.1.0

Mina: That explains it. Short-term we should avoid changing upstream behavior. Two mitigation options: (A) make preview dedupe prefer req_id first if present, (B) patch router to preserve sampling_id and redeploy, (C) add temporary alias synonyms in billing SKU map so token factors don't diverge.

Samir: I vote A + C immediately. Changing preview merge is low risk and quick. SKU synonyms buys time while router fix ships.

Viktor: Agreed. Also add a dashboard card comparing preview_vs_final_token_delta_pct by tenant with a 5% x 30m alert. We had too many silent rollouts.

Cara: I'll open a console ticket to add the UI field showing "alias_used_by_preview" vs "alias_used_by_billing" on the invoice preview page so CS can trace differences.

billing-bot: Created BILL-3710: "preview/final token delta - fallback rewrite" assigned to @Mina. Link: https://billing.redwood/tickets/BILL-3710

Mina: Plan: (1) patch preview merge to prefer req_id dedupe and deploy to canary in 2h, (2) add temporary alias synonyms for quant SKUs in sku_map (billing) today, (3) run scoped recompute of preview aggregates for affected window for tenants in BILL-3710 CSV, (4) patch router to preserve sampling_id and add contract test.

Samir: I'll produce CSV of affected tenants with this query:
```sql
SELECT tenant_id, req_id, SUM(tokens) as preview_tokens, COUNT(DISTINCT sampling_id) as sampling_buckets
FROM preview.aggregates
WHERE window_start >= '2026-06-14T01:00:00Z' AND window_end <= '2026-06-14T03:00:00Z'
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM raw.events e WHERE e.req_id = preview.aggregates.req_id)
GROUP BY tenant_id, req_id
HAVING SUM(tokens) > 0 AND COUNT(DISTINCT sampling_id) > 1
LIMIT 500;
```

Samir: CSV to BILL-3710 in 30m.

Viktor: Postmortem actions: document dedupe precedence (req_id > sampling_id > route_tag/model_alias), add e2e test that forces fallback while carrying sampling_id, and add a rollout checklist item: "verify sampling_id preservation for fallback normalization".

Cara: Agree. Also add an annotation in the Console next to invoice_preview: "Preview counts may differ from final due to routing normalization/discounts. Click for audit."

Mina: I'll run the recompute once patch is verified in canary and attach per-req diffs for support.

Samir: one more small ask: add an internal alert when router-normalizer change touches fields: sampling_id, req_id, model_alias. We can gate major changes behind a METRICS smoke-check.

deploy-bot: Noted. I'll include a preflight check in the next deploy for router that verifies all headers are preserved for a sample of 1000 synthetic requests.

Viktor: Great. Thanks team. Let's reconvene after canary verification. :thumbsup:
